title: Subnet Shield Blueprint: Terraform module for VPC subnet topology, egress shaping, endpoints and upgrade safety
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Create a new opinionated Terraform module (subnet-shield) that implements a repeatable VPC subnet topology tailored for Redwood Private deployments. The module will standardize AZ-aware subnet tiling, deterministic NAT/IGW egress placement, a VPC endpoint catalog (S3, ECR, SSM, Secrets Manager, optional KMS proxy), and explicit route table wiring for egress, service endpoints, and managed transit. The module must be idempotent, support safe in-place upgrades with automated plan-time checks, and expose hooks for synthetic health probes and CDN/NAT failover policies. Aim to reduce bespoke per-customer VPC templates and make upgrades predictable with built-in drift detection and canary upgrade support.
acceptance_criteria: Module deploys identical baseline topology in two test AWS accounts using same inputs with no drift after 3 apply cycles
Canary upgrade workflow: patch a single AZ subnet routing and verify synthetic egress and endpoint health for 30 minutes before rolling to remaining AZs
Automated Terraform plan-time blocker rejects destructive changes to NAT/IGW and endpoint policies unless explicit opt-in flag is set
Module publishes example usage (1) minimal single-AZ dev, (2) multi-AZ production with KMS proxy and private ECR endpoints
Healthcheck integration: outputs include route table IDs and a small cloudwatch-synthetics template that validates endpoint connectivity
Module passes security review checklist (KMS access least-privilege, endpoint policies locked down, secrets never stored in state)
Unit tests with terraform-compliance/terratest validate resource naming, tag schema, and cross-AZ CIDR allocation logic
tasks: Design module interface: inputs/outputs and sane defaults (subnet_counts_by_az, nat_strategy, endpoint_whitelist)
Implement core resources: aws_vpc, aws_subnet (public/private/isolated), aws_internet_gateway, aws_nat_gateway or NAT instance option
Implement endpoint set: aws_vpc_endpoint for S3, DynamoDB (if requested), ECR, CloudWatch Logs, SSM, Secrets Manager; KMS proxy as optional
Route table orchestration: explicit maps for egress, endpoint prefix lists, and cross-AZ stable associations
Add plan-time checks: a pre-apply validation script (terraform validate + custom python check) to detect risky egress changes
Add synthetic health probes: CloudWatch Synthetics blueprint and a small lambda that checks route connectivity and endpoint reachability
Implement canary upgrade helpers: module flag canary_az and small wrapper to run canary applies
Add drift detection: periodic TF plan job in CI that creates alerts for unexpected diffs
Write example stacks: dev, staging, prod with documented variables and upgrade steps
Prepare docs: module README, upgrade guide, rollback instructions, and security notes
Create unit/integration tests: terratest suites and terraform-compliance feature files
Open PR with module and CI jobs; request security & infra review

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: In-place changes to NAT/IGW could cause transient egress interruptions. Mitigation: default to create-new-then-swap where possible and require force_opt_in to destroy egress resources.
Risk: Endpoint policy misconfiguration could expose S3 buckets. Mitigation: ship restrictive policy templates and require security_review_required=true for enabling broad endpoints.

Risk: Terraform state drift from external changes. Mitigation: add periodic plan diffs, document manual reconciliation steps, and provide scripts to import existing resources into module-managed state
